name: Isshiah
overview: Isshiah was a male Levite known as the son of Rehabiah, who was the son of Eliezer, the son of Moses, establishing his direct descent from the great leader and prophet Moses. His lineage places him within the tribe of Levi, the priestly tribe of Israel, highlighting his connection to the sacred duties entrusted to this family line. There are no additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Isshiah means 'y-h-v-h forgets,' reflecting a Hebrew theophoric element referencing the LORD. Additionally, the name Jeshaiah, which means 'y-h-v-h will save,' is associated with him in Scripture, indicating a close linguistic and thematic connection between these names, both rooted in the covenant name of God.
familyAndRelationships: Isshiah is explicitly recorded as the son of Rehabiah, who was the son of Eliezer, descending from Moses, establishing a clear paternal lineage. There is also an inferred relationship that Joram was his father, though this is less certain. Scripture thus provides a direct genealogical context for Isshiah within the Levitical family line.
scriptureSignificance: Isshiah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical connection to Moses, a foundational figure in Israel's history and God's redemptive plan. As a descendant of Moses through the tribe of Levi, Isshiah represents the continuation of the priestly heritage and the faithful transmission of God's covenant. His mention in the genealogical records underscores the importance of preserving the lineage of those who served in the sanctuary and maintained the worship of the LORD.
